display.purpose: Hero headlines over full-bleed photography only. Never in body copy or cards.

headline.purpose: Section-level h2 headings on light and dark section backgrounds.

title.purpose: Card titles, athlete names, modal headings (h3/h4).

body.purpose: Athlete bios, campaign descriptions, editorial content. Aim 65–75ch on full-width blocks.

label.purpose: Section eyebrows (uppercase, 0.08em tracking) and bold micro-labels (sentence case, 0.01em tracking).

shadows.name: card-ambient
shadows.purpose: Card rest state (.card-lift). A whisper — separates card from page without announcing itself.

shadows.name: card-hover
shadows.purpose: Card hover state (.card-lift-hover), paired with translateY(-2px) at 280ms ease.

shadows.name: btn-primary-glow
shadows.purpose: Primary button warm underlay glow. Structural, not atmospheric.

shadows.name: icon-badge
shadows.purpose: Icon medallion boxes that sit proud of the card surface.

motion.name: ken-burns
motion.purpose: Slow cinematic drift on hero background photography. scale(1.04)→scale(1.12). Disabled on prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: Scroll reveal for sections: fade from opacity:0 + translateY(28px) to visible. Disabled on prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: card-hover-lift
motion.purpose: Card hover transition: shadow deepens + translateY(-2px).

motion.name: btn-transition
motion.purpose: All button state transitions (color, shadow, scale).

motion.name: pulse-live
motion.purpose: Live-funding status dot: pulses between opacity:1/scale:1 and opacity:0.55/scale:0.85.

motion.name: scroll-cue
motion.purpose: Bobbing chevron at hero bottom: translateY 0→6px, opacity 0.85→0.4.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Slightly springy exit easing for reveal transitions.

narrative.overview:
Athlete Arc is bold and honest by design. It does not soften — it declares. Every surface is built around the athlete's face and story first, with funding mechanics subordinated to the narrative. The typography is heavy-set Montserrat at near-display weight for headlines, pairing an urgent, athletic voice with the calm precision of Inter for body text. Generous whitespace keeps the visual hierarchy uncluttered even when content is dense.

Champion Orange is the system's single spark — a vivid, high-chroma signal (#ff5f1f) reserved for the moments that demand action: primary CTAs, funding progress, highlighted achievements. Podium Blue provides trustworthy counterweight, carrying secondary actions and verified information. Stadium Charcoal grounds everything in legible authority. Photography is always the first visual layer; color and type build on top of it, never in competition.

The system is deeply photographic and dark-section–friendly. Hero areas use full-bleed imagery with dark gradient overlays, film grain texture, and a slow Ken Burns drift — a cinematic frame for athletic pursuit. Scroll-triggered reveals (fade + rise) and purposeful hover states (lift + translate) give the interface tactile confidence without crossing into showmanship.
keyCharacteristics: Story-first at every level: athlete name, sport, and photo before any funding metric
Two-tone authority: Champion Orange ignites; Podium Blue anchors; Stadium Charcoal grounds
Pill-shaped interaction language — buttons, badges, and progress bars share the same curved form
Flat surfaces with earned elevation: only hover and state produce depth
Photography-backed dark sections for hero moments; cool-paper light sections for content

rules.name: The Orange Reserve Rule
rules.body: Champion Orange Vivid (#ff5f1f) appears on ≤10% of any given screen's surface area. Its scarcity is the point — the eye lands on it immediately and knows it is actionable.

rules.name: The Story-First Rule
rules.body: Athlete name, sport, and photograph appear before any funding metric or supporter count on every athlete-facing surface.

rules.name: The No-Italic Rule
rules.body: Italic type is absent from this system. Emphasis is achieved through weight contrast (700 vs. 400) and color, never slant.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Ceiling
rules.body: Uppercase-tracked eyebrows are reserved for section kickers only. Never apply the eyebrow style to interactive elements or paragraph text.

rules.name: The Flat-Default Rule
rules.body: A surface at rest has no shadow. Elevation is a verb, not a property.

rules.name: The Pill Covenant
rules.body: All interactive primitives — buttons, badges, progress bars, chips — use border-radius: 9999px. Square and angular corners are absent from the interactive layer.

dos: Do lead with the athlete's name, sport, and photograph before any funding metric or follower count on every athlete-facing surface.
Do use Champion Orange Vivid (#ff5f1f) only for primary CTAs, progress fills, and funding-moment accents — scarcity is its power.
Do apply rounded-pill (9999px) to all interactive primitives: buttons, badges, chips, and progress bars.
Do show cost line items whenever a campaign is presented — transparency is the product, not a feature.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion — disable Ken Burns, scroll-cue, reveal, and card-lift-hover transitions.
Do use Podium Blue (#0453cd) for all focus rings — consistent, accessible, and visually distinct from orange.
donts: Don't use Champion Orange Vivid for decorative purposes — every orange moment must signal action or a funding milestone.
Don't use italic type — emphasis is weight (700 vs 400) and color, never slant.
Don't place funding metrics, supporter counts, or raised amounts before the athlete's story on any primary surface.
Don't add fields, steps, or configuration options to onboarding and campaign flows without explicit justification — minimalism is a constraint, not a preference.
Don't apply shadows to surfaces at rest — elevation is a response to state, not a standing property.
Don't use the uppercase eyebrow style on interactive elements or inline in paragraph copy.
